review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

12:1.sourceText: Παρακαλῶ οὖν ὑμᾶς, ἀδελφοί, διὰ τῶν οἰκτιρμῶν τοῦ Θεοῦ παραστῆσαι τὰ σώματα ὑμῶν θυσίαν ζῶσαν ἁγίαν τῷ Θεῷ εὐάρεστον, τὴν λογικὴν λατρείαν ὑμῶν·
12:1.targetText: Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God’s mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship.

groups.note: The predicate accusative θυσίαν ("a sacrifice") supplies as … sacrifices.
The article τήν introducing the apposition is rendered which.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the adjectives with and; the Greek has no καί here.
English supplies a copula in the appositional phrase.

12:2.sourceText: καὶ μὴ συνσχηματίζεσθε τῷ αἰῶνι τούτῳ, ἀλλὰ μεταμορφοῦσθε τῇ ἀνακαινώσει τοῦ νοός, εἰς τὸ δοκιμάζειν ὑμᾶς τί τὸ θέλημα τοῦ Θεοῦ, τὸ ἀγαθὸν καὶ εὐάρεστον καὶ τέλειον.
12:2.targetText: Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what is the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God.

groups.note: Same verb; BSB's Greek text has another form of it here, with the same meaning.
The article τοῦ ("the" mind) is rendered your.
εἰς τό with the infinitive marks the result, rendered Then.

targetPhrases.text: will be able to test and approve

groups.note: δοκιμάζειν ("to test, to approve") in the result clause is rendered will be able to test and approve.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the opening καί ("and") untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB lists the adjectives with a comma in place of this καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the question what … will of God.

12:3.sourceText: Λέγω γὰρ διὰ τῆς χάριτος τῆς δοθείσης μοι παντὶ τῷ ὄντι ἐν ὑμῖν, μὴ ὑπερφρονεῖν παρ’ ὃ δεῖ φρονεῖν, ἀλλὰ φρονεῖν εἰς τὸ σωφρονεῖν, ἑκάστῳ ὡς ὁ Θεὸς ἐμέρισεν μέτρον πίστεως.
12:3.targetText: For by the grace given me I say to every one of you: Do not think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think of yourself with sober judgment, according to the measure of faith God has given you.

groups.note: ἐν ("among") is rendered of.
ὑπερφρονεῖν ("to think too highly") is rendered Do … think … more highly.
παρ’ ὅ ("beyond what") is rendered than.
εἰς τό with the infinitive ("so as to") is rendered with.
ἑκάστῳ ("to each") is rendered you.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB renders τῷ ὄντι ἐν ὑμῖν ("who is among you") as of you, with no word for the participle ὄντι ("being").
BSB leaves the repeated φρονεῖν ("to think") unexpressed after ought.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies an object for think.
English supplies a subject for the impersonal δεῖ ("it is necessary").
English supplies an object for think.

12:4.sourceText: καθάπερ γὰρ ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι πολλὰ μέλη ἔχομεν, τὰ δὲ μέλη πάντα οὐ τὴν αὐτὴν ἔχει πρᾶξιν,
12:4.targetText: Just as each of us has one body with many members, and not all members have the same function,

groups.note: BSB recasts ἐν ἑνὶ σώματι ("in one body") as one body with.
ἔχομεν ("we have") is rendered us … has.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective γάρ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English adds each of; the Greek verb says only "we have".

12:5.sourceText: οὕτως οἱ πολλοὶ ἓν σῶμά ἐσμεν ἐν Χριστῷ, τὸ δὲ καθ’ εἷς ἀλλήλων μέλη.
12:5.targetText: so in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another.

groups.note: The article οἱ ("the" many) is rendered who.
τὸ καθ’ εἷς ("one by one, individually") is rendered each.
The genitive ἀλλήλων ("of one another") is rendered belongs to one another.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the phrase who are many.

12:6.sourceText: ἔχοντες δὲ χαρίσματα κατὰ τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσαν ἡμῖν διάφορα, εἴτε προφητείαν, κατὰ τὴν ἀναλογίαν τῆς πίστεως·
12:6.targetText: We have different gifts according to the grace given us. If one’s gift is prophecy, let him use it in proportion to his faith;

groups.note: The participle ἔχοντες ("having") is rendered have.
The article τῆς ("the" faith) is rendered his.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject for the participle ἔχοντες ("having").
English supplies a frame for the gift named after εἴτε ("whether").
English supplies a command; the Greek clause has no verb.

12:7.sourceText: εἴτε διακονίαν, ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ· εἴτε ὁ διδάσκων, ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ·
12:7.targetText: if it is serving, let him serve; if it is teaching, let him teach;

groups.note: διακονίᾳ ("service") is rendered as the verb serve.
ὁ διδάσκων ("the one who teaches") is rendered teaching.
διδασκαλίᾳ ("teaching") is rendered as the verb teach.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts ἐν τῇ διακονίᾳ ("in the serving") as a verb, so ἐν and the article have no separate English.
BSB recasts ἐν τῇ διδασκαλίᾳ ("in the teaching") as a verb, so ἐν and the article have no separate English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula after if.
English supplies a command; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies a subject and copula after if.
English supplies a command; the Greek clause has no verb.

12:8.sourceText: εἴτε ὁ παρακαλῶν, ἐν τῇ παρακλήσει· ὁ μεταδιδοὺς ἐν ἁπλότητι, ὁ προϊστάμενος ἐν σπουδῇ, ὁ ἐλεῶν ἐν ἱλαρότητι.
12:8.targetText: if it is encouraging, let him encourage; if it is giving, let him give generously; if it is leading, let him lead with diligence; if it is showing mercy, let him do it cheerfully.

groups.note: ὁ παρακαλῶν ("the one who encourages") is rendered encouraging.
παρακλήσει ("encouragement") is rendered as the verb encourage.
ὁ μεταδιδούς ("the one who gives") is rendered giving, and BSB repeats its verb as give.
ἐν ἁπλότητι ("in generosity") is rendered generously.
ὁ προϊστάμενος ("the one who leads") is rendered leading, and BSB repeats its verb as lead.
ὁ ἐλεῶν ("the one who shows mercy") is rendered showing mercy, and BSB refers back to it with do it.
ἐν ἱλαρότητι ("in cheerfulness") is rendered cheerfully.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB recasts ἐν τῇ παρακλήσει ("in the encouraging") as a verb, so ἐν and the article have no separate English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula after if.
English supplies a command; the Greek clause has no verb.
BSB continues the if-it-is frame; the Greek has no εἴτε here.
English supplies a command for the person giving.
BSB continues the if-it-is frame; the Greek has no εἴτε here.
English supplies a command for the person leading.
BSB continues the if-it-is frame; the Greek has no εἴτε here.
English supplies a command for the person showing mercy.

12:9.sourceText: ἡ ἀγάπη ἀνυπόκριτος. ἀποστυγοῦντες τὸ πονηρόν, κολλώμενοι τῷ ἀγαθῷ·
12:9.targetText: Love must be sincere. Detest what is evil; cling to what is good.

groups.note: The article τό ("the" evil) is rendered what.
The article τῷ ("the" good) is rendered what.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a command frame; the Greek has the adjective ἀνυπόκριτος ("sincere") with no verb.
English supplies a copula in the phrase what is evil.
English supplies a copula in the phrase what is good.

12:10.sourceText: τῇ φιλαδελφίᾳ εἰς ἀλλήλους φιλόστοργοι, τῇ τιμῇ ἀλλήλους προηγούμενοι,
12:10.targetText: Be devoted to one another in brotherly love. Outdo yourselves in honoring one another.

groups.note: προηγούμενοι ("leading the way") is rendered Outdo.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a command frame; the Greek has the adjective φιλόστοργοι ("devoted") with no verb.
English supplies an object for Outdo.

12:11.sourceText: τῇ σπουδῇ μὴ ὀκνηροί, τῷ πνεύματι ζέοντες, τῷ Κυρίῳ δουλεύοντες,
12:11.targetText: Do not let your zeal subside; keep your spiritual fervor, serving the Lord.

groups.note: The article τῇ ("the" zeal) is rendered your.
The adjective ὀκνηροί ("lazy, slack") is rendered with the verb subside.
The article τῷ ("the" spirit) is rendered your.
The participle ζέοντες ("being fervent") is rendered keep … fervor.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a command frame; the Greek has the adjective ὀκνηροί with no verb.
English supplies a command frame; the Greek has the adjective ὀκνηροί with no verb.

12:12.sourceText: τῇ ἐλπίδι χαίροντες, τῇ θλίψει ὑπομένοντες, τῇ προσευχῇ προσκαρτεροῦντες,
12:12.targetText: Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer.

groups.note: The participle χαίροντες ("rejoicing") is rendered Be joyful.
The participle ὑπομένοντες ("enduring") is rendered patient.
The participle προσκαρτεροῦντες ("persisting") is rendered persistent.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:13.sourceText: ταῖς χρείαις τῶν ἁγίων κοινωνοῦντες, τὴν φιλοξενίαν διώκοντες.
12:13.targetText: Share with the saints who are in need. Practice hospitality.

groups.note: χρείαις ("needs") is rendered in need.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a relative clause for the saints' needs.

12:14.sourceText: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς διώκοντας, εὐλογεῖτε καὶ μὴ καταρᾶσθε.
12:14.targetText: Bless those who persecute you. Bless and do not curse.

unmappedTarget.reason: BSB follows a reading with an extra word here; N1904 has no object for persecute.

12:15.sourceText: χαίρειν μετὰ χαιρόντων, κλαίειν μετὰ κλαιόντων.
12:15.targetText: Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep.

12:16.sourceText: τὸ αὐτὸ εἰς ἀλλήλους φρονοῦντες· μὴ τὰ ὑψηλὰ φρονοῦντες ἀλλὰ τοῖς ταπεινοῖς συναπαγόμενοι. μὴ γίνεσθε φρόνιμοι παρ’ ἑαυτοῖς.
12:16.targetText: Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but enjoy the company of the lowly. Do not be conceited.

groups.note: τὸ αὐτὸ φρονοῦντες ("thinking the same thing") is rendered Live in harmony.
τὰ ὑψηλὰ φρονοῦντες ("thinking lofty things") is rendered Do … be proud.
συναπαγόμενοι ("associating with") is rendered enjoy the company of.
φρόνιμοι παρ’ ἑαυτοῖς ("wise in your own sight") is rendered conceited.

12:17.sourceText: μηδενὶ κακὸν ἀντὶ κακοῦ ἀποδιδόντες· προνοούμενοι καλὰ ἐνώπιον πάντων ἀνθρώπων·
12:17.targetText: Do not repay anyone evil for evil. Carefully consider what is right in the eyes of everybody.

groups.note: μηδενί ("to no one") is rendered not … anyone.
καλά ("good things") is rendered what … right.
πάντων ἀνθρώπων ("all people") is rendered everybody.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the phrase what is right.

12:18.sourceText: εἰ δυνατόν, τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν μετὰ πάντων ἀνθρώπων εἰρηνεύοντες·
12:18.targetText: If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone.

groups.note: τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν ("as far as it is from you") is rendered on your part.
πάντων ἀνθρώπων ("all people") is rendered everyone.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a subject and copula for δυνατόν ("possible").

12:19.sourceText: μὴ ἑαυτοὺς ἐκδικοῦντες, ἀγαπητοί, ἀλλὰ δότε τόπον τῇ ὀργῇ· γέγραπται γάρ Ἐμοὶ ἐκδίκησις, ἐγὼ ἀνταποδώσω, λέγει Κύριος.
12:19.targetText: Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath. For it is written: “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord.”

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English names whose wrath is meant; the Greek has the article only.
English supplies a copula in the saying Vengeance is Mine.

12:20.sourceText: ἀλλὰ ἐὰν πεινᾷ ὁ ἐχθρός σου, ψώμιζε αὐτόν· ἐὰν διψᾷ, πότιζε αὐτόν· τοῦτο γὰρ ποιῶν ἄνθρακας πυρὸς σωρεύσεις ἐπὶ τὴν κεφαλὴν αὐτοῦ.
12:20.targetText: On the contrary,  “If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink. For in so doing, you will heap burning coals on his head.”

groups.note: τοῦτο ("this") is rendered so in the phrase in so doing.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

12:21.sourceText: μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τοῦ κακοῦ, ἀλλὰ νίκα ἐν τῷ ἀγαθῷ τὸ κακόν.
12:21.targetText: Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
